_comment: StaXX -- the well-known database images table (PLAN_70 stage 5, 10.2). The single source of truth read by both the server (include/CrossLinks.php) and the browser (javascript/db-images.js) -- see either file for how. Guessing a secret from a setting's *name* is refused elsewhere in this project, so the only honest way to recognise 'this is the password box' for a handful of very common images is to say so outright, for images checked one at a time against their own documentation. Every setting name was verified against the image's Docker Hub page (and, for MariaDB, its own Knowledge Base) rather than recalled. Nothing here is inferred from a setting's spelling; it is either in this table or it is unknown. 'user'/'password'/'rootPassword'/'database' are each a priority-ordered list of the environment settings that image recognises -- first name found in the target's file wins. Left out on purpose: no MariaDB/MySQL 'random root password' or hashed-password variants, since they hold no password value to read.

images.note: The official image. From MariaDB 10.6 the MARIADB_* names are tried first, but the MYSQL_* names it grew out of still work -- this is MariaDB's own documented backward-compatibility promise, not a guess.
LinuxServer's rebuild only ever recognises the older MYSQL_* names -- setting a MARIADB_* one against this image does nothing, so it needs its own entry rather than sharing the official image's.
Percona Server for MySQL is a drop-in replacement and documents the identical MYSQL_* variables as the official mysql image.

Postgres has one account, not two -- POSTGRES_USER is the superuser, so there is no separate root slot to fill in. pgvecto-rs is a postgres rebuild whose own quick-start uses the same POSTGRES_* variables verbatim.
Mongo only ever creates the root account from these variables -- a plain, unprivileged user is application-created afterwards, not something an environment setting names.

The plain 'redis' image on Docker Hub documents no password environment variable at all -- only a mounted config file or a command-line --requirepass. Bitnami's rebuild is the common one that does take a setting, and it has no username at all: this is the password-only shape the plan calls for.
Same story as Bitnami's Redis rebuild: a password setting, no username. The official valkey/valkey image, like official redis, documents no environment variable for this at all.

The account is hard-wired to 'sa' -- there is no setting that names a username, only the one that sets its password -- so this is also password-only. (Older documentation called this variable SA_PASSWORD; current images require MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD.)
